title: Федеральный закон от 24.07.2023 № 339-ФЗ (amendments to Civil Code: legal regime of digital rubles)
issuer: Russian Federation (State Duma / Federation Council / President)
relevance: legal nature (digital rubles as non-cash funds); transfers by Bank of Russia on platform
content_note: Digital rubles defined as a type of non-cash funds; settlements by transfer of digital rubles by the Bank of Russia within the platform; inheritance rules.

title: Положение Банка России от 03.08.2023 № 820-П 'О платформе цифрового рубля' (platform rules)
relevance: architecture; operations (incl. smart contracts); access via participant banks
content_note: Platform rules regulation listed on cbr.ru 'Правила платформы цифрового рубля'; PDF is a scanned image (no text layer) - content not verified beyond title.

title: Цифровой рубль: старт пилота (press release)
relevance: status_decision (pilot with real digital rubles from 15 Aug 2023, 13 banks)
content_note: Testing with real digital rubles starts 15 Aug with 13 banks; mass rollout after phased testing; 'начиная с 2025 года' expected use by citizens and business.

title: Основные направления развития национальной платежной системы на период 2025-2027 годов
content_note: 'запланирована выработка общих подходов к реализации офлайн-режима цифрового рубля'; smart-contract development; phased budget operations in digital rubles from 2025.

title: Федеральный закон от 23.05.2025 № 105-ФЗ (AML/CFT regime for operations with digital rubles on the platform)
issuer: Russian Federation (State Duma / Federation Council / President)
relevance: data access (BoR AML monitoring, reporting to Rosfinmonitoring); identification by banks
content_note: Bank of Russia as platform operator must assess risk, freeze funds and report to Rosfinmonitoring; banks keep duty to identify platform users.

title: Массовое внедрение цифрового рубля начнется 1 сентября 2026 года (press release)
content_note: Largest banks must offer digital ruble operations from 1 Sept 2026; all banks phased by Sept 2028; law adopted by State Duma.

title: Федеральный закон от 23.07.2025 № 248-ФЗ (phased mass introduction of the digital ruble from 1 Sept 2026; universal payment code)
issuer: Russian Federation (State Duma / Federation Council / President)
content_note: Enters into force 1 Sept 2026: credit institutions offering e-payment means must enable digital ruble operations; phased 2026/2027/2028 by bank licence and merchant revenue.

title: Концепция платформы коммерческих смарт-контрактов (with press release of 18 June 2026)
content_note: Proposes a commercial smart-contract platform within digital ruble infrastructure, BoR as operator at first stage; comments invited until 30.09.2026. Press: https://www.cbr.ru/press/event/?id=32630

title: Операции с цифровым рублем будут бесплатны (interview with A. Bakina, Director NPS Department)
relevance: offline (planned, later stage); one wallet per person; architecture
content_note: Offline payments are a goal 'на следующих этапах', market study to finish autumn 2026 before testing; one account per person on BoR platform. Speaker is department director, not board member.

title: Цифровой рубль: старт использования (press release)
relevance: status_decision (general availability from 1 Sept 2026); holding/top-up limits; one account per person
content_note: From 1 Sept 2026 citizens may open a digital ruble account on the BoR platform; one account per person; top-up from bank accounts up to 300k rub/month.

title: Цифровой рубль - Вопросы и ответы (FAQ)
content_note: Information on citizens 'не превышает объем... по операциям с безналичными рублями'; balances protected by bank secrecy; no interest paid; rollout dates 2026-2028.

title: NBR Annual Financial Stability Report (2021/22) - CBDC paragraph
content_note: 'The NBR is currently studying and exploring whether the introduction of a CBDC could confer benefits...; once completed will inform on requirements, readiness, and next steps.' Weak, early status statement.

title: Research Paper on Rwanda Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) (feasibility study summary)
issuer: National Bank of Rwanda (in partnership with an external technology partner)
relevance: objectives (4 sweet spots); architecture (two-tier); token-based; offline; privacy; programmability/smart contracts; status (proceed iteratively)
content_note: Recommends a token-based model 'that supports online and offline transactions', two-tier distribution; privacy 'for honest users' with configurable levels; proceed 'iteratively and cautiously'.

title: Ibibazo bibazwa kenshi ku ifaranga-koranabuhanga (CBDC) - CBDC FAQs in Kinyarwanda
content_note: Kinyarwanda FAQ published with the 2024 research paper (dated 09/04/2024 on the CBDC page); earlier edition than the English 2025 FAQ. Content not checked in detail (language).

title: Rwanda National Financial Inclusion Roadmap 2025-2030 (action 4.5 'Explore a CBDC for Rwanda' / 4.5.1 'Pilot a CBDC in Rwanda')
issuer: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning and National Bank of Rwanda
relevance: status (planned CBDC pilot, NBR lead); objectives (inclusion)
content_note: Roadmap action 4.5.1 'Pilot a CBDC in Rwanda - Test inclusive CBDC user access methodologies and tools', lead NBR with FSPs, RSwitch, MINICT, MINALOC. Exact publication date not verified.

title: Frequently Asked Questions - FAQs about CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency)
relevance: objectives (resilience to outages, cashless, remittances); status (exploration concluded 2024, now PoC); account vs token
content_note: 'exploration research which was concluded in 2024 now progressing into a proof of concept'; PoC 'will inform the decisions for further live pilots or a differentiated stance'.

title: CBDC page (Financial Innovation > CBDC): feasibility study summary and 'sweet spots'
content_note: Summarises feasibility study: sweet spots = resilience against network outages/power failures, innovation and competition, cashless economy, cheaper cross-border remittances; lists all CBDC documents.

title: The Riksbank's e-krona project, Report 2
relevance: architecture (value- vs account-based); anonymity; legal mandate; objectives
content_note: Sets out value-based vs account-based e-krona; 'Anonymous payments are possible with a value-based e-krona' (s.3.5); legislative amendments needed for Riksbank mandate.

title: E-krona pilot phase 1
relevance: ledger technology (DLT/blockchain); token-based; offline; holding limits/interest
content_note: Tested e-krona 'token-based in a distributed network based on blockchain technology'; local storage of tokens and off-line payments; token model with balance cap and interest.

title: Payments Report 2022 - 'The Riksbank is making preparations for a possible e-krona'
content_note: Objective: preserve public access to government money and resilience; 'No decision has yet been taken to issue an e-krona.' (Earlier editions 2019-2021 have similar sections.)

title: E-krona pilot phase 2
relevance: ledger (DLT/Corda); token-based; offline; integration with payment infrastructure; legal status
content_note: DLT- and token-based solution on Corda enables a parallel e-krona network; token-based offline solution tested; integration with participants' systems.

title: Staten och betalningarna (SOU 2023:16), final report of the Payments Inquiry
issuer: Government Offices of Sweden (parliamentary Payments Inquiry, Ministry of Finance)
relevance: status (no sufficient societal need for e-krona at present; reassess later)
content_note: Inquiry assessed 'insufficient social need for the Riksbank to issue an e-krona' but global changes may lead to a different assessment (as summarised on riksbank.se). Government channel; not opened in full.

title: E-krona pilot phase 3
relevance: programmability (conditional payments); privacy/data sharing; access model/governance
content_note: Conditional payments tested but 'can mean that more data on the users is shared ... important ... to protect personal integrity'; access via payment service providers with governance options.

title: Work on e-krona entering new phase (news)
relevance: status_decision (technical pilot concluded; focus on requirements for an issuable e-krona and digital euro)
content_note: 'As the work on an e-krona enters a new phase, the pilot project is brought to a conclusion'; Riksbank to focus on consequences/requirements of an issuable e-krona and legal amendments.

title: Consultation response regarding The state and payments (SOU 2023:16)
relevance: status (legislation for possible e-krona must begin now; no issuance decision)
content_note: 'work on producing legislation for a possible e-krona must begin now'; 'not a question of deciding whether an e-krona should be issued or not, but of being prepared'.

title: Political decisions needed urgently so that everyone can pay (press release, Payments Report 2023)
relevance: status (call to prepare e-krona legislation); objectives
content_note: 'The Riksbank considers that legislative work on a possible e-krona needs to begin now', citing the Commission's digital euro proposal and ECB preparation phase.

title: Payments Report 2024 - 'Work on the e-krona continues'
relevance: status; legislation preparation; digital euro linkage
content_note: 'The Riksbank's work on an e-krona continues'; e-krona as new infrastructure for competition, cross-border payments and preparedness; technical pilot concluded. Registry holds only 2025/2026 editions.

title: E-krona pilot phase 4: offline payments with e-krona
relevance: offline (balance-based shadow-wallet solution); status (no decision on issuance/design)
content_note: Tested secure balance-based offline solution (shadow wallet, payment card); 'There is currently no decision on issuing an e-krona, how an e-krona might be designed or what technology might be used.'

title: Letter to the Committee on Finance - information on developments that bring the issue of a digital krona to the fore (official communication, Dnr 2026-01419)
relevance: status (no position taken; issuance needs Riksdag consent; legislative timeframe); objectives (resilience, sovereignty); offline
content_note: 'The Riksbank has not taken a position on whether a digital krona should be issued'; a digital krona would 'offer enhanced opportunities to make offline payments'; informs Riksdag on timeframe and legislation. Published 15 Oct 2026; Swedish edition exists.

title: Reply to Parliamentary Question on the implementation progress of Project Ubin
issuer: Monetary Authority of Singapore / Parliament of Singapore
relevance: retail vs wholesale distinction; risks (bank disintermediation); status
content_note: 'A retail CBDC ... is essentially a deposit held directly with the central bank. If a retail CBDC becomes pervasive, it could have significant implications for banks' deposit...' (mainly wholesale Ubin context).

title: MAS Partners IMF, World Bank and others to launch Global Challenge for Retail CBDC Solutions (media release)
relevance: objectives (public policy objectives for retail CBDC design: inclusion, resilience, integrity, stability)
content_note: Retail CBDC 'has the potential to increase payments efficiencies, improve financial inclusion'; design must meet public policy objectives incl. resilience/integrity and monetary/financial stability.

title: A Retail Central Bank Digital Currency: Economic Considerations in the Singapore Context
issuer: Monetary Authority of Singapore (Economic Policy Group)
relevance: status (no pressing need; exploratory work); privacy; holding limits; remuneration; intermediation; offline
content_note: 'no pressing need for a retail CBDC in Singapore at this point in time'; could let users 'control their transaction data and preserve their privacy'; hard limits; private distribution; offline possible (pre-funded).

title: 'The Future of Money, Finance and the Internet' - speech by Ravi Menon, MD, at Singapore FinTech Festival
relevance: objectives (reasons for a digital SGD); status (paper released; exploration)
content_note: Sets out 'three possible reasons for MAS to issue to the public a digital Singapore dollar' (central bank money online, etc.) alongside the Nov 2021 retail CBDC paper.

title: Reply to COS Cut on Digital Sing Dollar (parliamentary reply by Minister Lawrence Wong on behalf of SM Tharman, Minister in charge of MAS)
issuer: Monetary Authority of Singapore / Parliament of Singapore
relevance: status_decision (retail CBDC case 'not compelling'; not ruled out; Orchid builds capability)
content_note: 'MAS has assessed that the case for a retail CBDC in Singapore is not compelling'; 'does not mean that MAS has ruled out introducing a retail CBDC'; will continue to prepare.

title: 'Money at a Crossroads: Public or Private Digital Money?' - panel remarks by Ravi Menon at IMF seminar
relevance: status (open mind; no compelling case yet)
content_note: 'For retail CBDCs, MAS is keeping an open mind... But there does not seem to be a compelling case for it yet'.

title: 'Yes to Digital Asset Innovation, No to Cryptocurrency Speculation' - opening address by Ravi Menon, Green Shoots Seminar
relevance: status (not compelling; building infrastructure via Orchid)
content_note: 'The case for a retail CBDC in Singapore is not compelling for now'; MAS building technology infrastructure to permit issuance 'should conditions change'.

title: Purpose Bound Money (PBM) Technical Whitepaper (with media release 'MAS Proposes Standards for Digital Money')
relevance: programmability (common protocol for conditions on CBDC/tokenised deposits/stablecoins)
content_note: Proposes a common protocol 'to specify conditions for the use of digital money such as CBDCs, tokenised bank deposits, and stablecoins on a distributed ledger' (Project Orchid follow-up). Not retail-CBDC-specific.

title: Orchid Blueprint: Infrastructure for safe and innovative use of digital money (with media release 'MAS Lays Foundation for Safe and Innovative Use of Digital Money in Singapore')
relevance: programmability (PBM protocol); ledger/infrastructure; status (MAS promotes wholesale CBDC, tokenised deposits, stablecoins - not retail CBDC)
content_note: Blueprint sets infrastructure 'required for a digital Singapore dollar'; release: 'three forms of digital money that MAS is promoting are wholesale CBDCs, tokenised bank liabilities, and regulated stablecoins'. Release: https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2023/mas-lays-foundation-for-safe-and-innovative-use-of-digital-money-in-singapore

title: Eswatini CBDC Diagnostic Study: Phase 1 findings
issuer: Central Bank of Eswatini (with Cenfri; Governor's foreword)
content_note: Ranks CBDC use cases (payment efficiency, consumer demand, stability); Governor's foreword; remaining phases paused pending Payment Switch. Authored by Cenfri for CBE.

title: Press release: Central Bank of Eswatini partners with Giesecke+Devrient to research and explore Eswatini's central bank-issued digital currency
content_note: Diagnostic found retail CBDC strongest opportunity; Digital Lilangeni investigated 'as a complement to cash'; design to cover governance, accessibility, interoperability, security and programmability.

title: CBDC Briefing (CBDC Explainer)
content_note: 'The Bank has not yet decided whether to introduce one'; sets project objectives: design principles, use cases, distribution model, technical and legal design; PoC and pilot planned.

title: Initial Design Paper for the Digital Lilangeni (final pre-pilot, DV07)
issuer: Central Bank of Eswatini with Giesecke+Devrient
relevance: privacy/anonymity; offline; distribution model (two-tier hybrid); ledger; objectives
content_note: Earlier edition of the 2024 paper: 'the CBE will proceed with partial pseudo-anonymity within the privacy design'; smart-card offline payments; two-tier hybrid model.

title: Initial Design Paper for the Digital Lilangeni (for stakeholder comments)
issuer: Central Bank of Eswatini with Giesecke+Devrient
content_note: Stakeholder-consultation draft (dated 25 May 2023, uploaded 2023-06-09) of the initial design paper; same privacy/offline sections as DV07.

title: Annual Integrated Report 2022/23 (CBDC section)
content_note: Reports G+D engagement after diagnostic found retail CBDC strongest opportunity; continued investigation of a Digital Lilangeni as complement to cash.

title: Governor's speech: Presentation of the 2022/23 Annual Integrated Report (2 Oct 2023)
content_note: Digital Lilangeni explored 'as a complement to cash'; lessons from project: local context, fees and speed as user pain points, early stakeholder engagement.

title: Annual Integrated Report 2023/24 (section: Central Bank Digital Currency: Digital Lilangeni Project)
relevance: pilot; offline (USSD, smart card); privacy vs transparency; non-interest-bearing; legal tender
content_note: Reports PoC and pilot with one FSP; USSD use without internet; limited offline testing; 'critical ... to establish balance between privacy and transparency'; non-interest bearing.

title: Governor's Presentation of the 2023/24 Annual Integrated Report (speech, 28 Aug 2024)
content_note: Bank completed CBDC R&D and 'determined that a full CBDC launch will not be pursued at this time', citing readiness concerns and the national payment switch.

title: Annual Integrated Report 2024/25 (section: Central Bank Digital Currency)
relevance: status (R&D completed); privacy balance; wholesale cross-border (Sunbird) noted
content_note: After completion of CBDC R&D, Bank published Design Paper Aug 2024 incl. 'appropriate balance between privacy and regulatory oversight'; Project Sunbird is wholesale.

title: CBDC (project web page, incl. 'Next Steps')
relevance: status_decision; objectives; offline; privacy; distribution model
content_note: CBE completed R&D and 'has decided not to proceed with issuing a CBDC at the moment'; pilot tested online/offline; privacy protections. Created 2021-10, modified 2025-11-28.

title: Frequently Asked Questions (CBDC section)
content_note: 'The Bank has yet to decide whether to issue a retail CBDC'; working group established after 2019 diagnostic. Undated and apparently outdated relative to the CBDC page.

title: The Way Forward for Retail Central Bank Digital Currency in Thailand (consultation paper)
relevance: objectives; holding/transaction limits; non-interest; programmability; intermediated distribution
content_note: Public consultation (comments by 15 June 2021): proposes cash-like, non-interest-bearing CBDC 'with specified limits for holding, transacting'; open to private-sector programmability.

title: Press release No. 21/2021: The Way Forward for Retail CBDC in Thailand
content_note: Retail CBDC 'can be used in financial transactions both online and offline'; main objective is convenient, secure access to financial services; invites public feedback.

title: Retail CBDC: Implications on Monetary Policy and Financial Stability in Thailand (study, English summary)
content_note: Concludes retail CBDC 'should not bear interest and should have certain holding or conversion limits'; distributed by intermediaries to protect deposits and stability.

title: Press release No. 60/2021: Retail CBDC: Implications on the Thai Financial Sector and Survey Results
relevance: consultation results; design (cash-like, non-interest, intermediaries, conversion limits); pilot plan
content_note: Survey/focus groups support BOT approach; key design: cash-like non-interest-bearing, intermediated distribution, conversion limits; Foundation and Innovation pilot tracks announced.

title: Repositioning Thailand's Financial Sector for a Sustainable Digital Economy (consultation paper, Financial Landscape)
content_note: Plans retail CBDC pilot around end-2022 as open infrastructure; asks public about programmable conditional payments (e.g. welfare distribution).

title: Press release No. 39/2022: Progress of Retail CBDC Development
relevance: status_decision (pilot; no issuance plan); programmability; privacy (vendor choice)
content_note: Pilot with ~10,000 users; Innovation track on programmability; 'the BOT does not have plans to issue Retail CBDC'; G+D chosen partly for 'data privacy and security'.

title: Press release No. 61/2565: Key points from BOT Digital Finance Conference 2022 (retail CBDC progress)
content_note: BOT 'has no plan yet to issue Retail CBDC'; limited pilot with private sector from December 2022; hackathon on programmability use cases (100+ teams).

title: Annual Report 2022 (retail CBDC section)
content_note: BOT 'has no plan to issue retail CBDC for the general public'; pilot with ~10,000 users and three firms for cash-like activities.

title: Annual Report 2023 (Box 5: The Progress of CBDC)
content_note: Pilot ran late 2022 to Oct 2023 as open-access infrastructure for banks and non-banks; BOT 'does not yet have a plan to issue the retail CBDC'.

title: Retail CBDC Pilot Program: Conclusion Report and Plan (landing page)
content_note: 'The BOT has no immediate plan to officially issue Retail CBDC'; pilot results used for technology design and future payment studies. Landing page for registry report.

title: Annual Report 2024 (Retail CBDC Pilot section)
content_note: Pilot: 4,000 users, 140 merchants, 55,695 transactions; BOT 'currently has no immediate plans to officially issue a retail CBDC for general use'.

title: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) web page incl. Retail CBDC section and FAQ
content_note: 'The Bank of Thailand currently has no plans to issue a Retail CBDC for general use'; FAQ lists benefits incl. programmable payment. Page undated (redesigned 2025-26); date before 2026-10-18 unverified.

title: Press Release on Central Bank Digital Turkish Lira R&D Project (2021-40)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
relevance: status_decision (no final decision; pilot); ledger technology (DLT/blockchain tests); objectives
content_note: 'The CBRT has made no final decision regarding the issuance'; prototype network and closed-circuit pilot; tests on blockchain, distributed ledgers, instant-payment integration; DTL to complement existing payments.

title: Press Release on the Use of Digital Turkish Lira (2022-55)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
relevance: pilot status; ledger technology; identity (digital identification)
content_note: First payments on the DTL Network; pilots continue in 2023; DLT and instant-payment integration tests; 'digital identification is of critical importance for the project'.

title: Dijital Türk Lirası Birinci Faz Değerlendirme Raporuna İlişkin Basın Duyurusu (2023-56)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
content_note: Announces Phase 1 Evaluation Report; phase 1 pilot measured user experience and system performance at selected locations. Cover note for registry report.

title: Annual Report 2023 (DTL passages)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
content_note: PoC studies on programmable payments, e-commerce, international, offline payments and hybrid systems; first phase pilot ended H1 2023.

title: Governor Fatih Karahan's Presentation on '24 Fintech' (Riyadh), slides
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (Governor)
content_note: Slides 'CBDCs: CBRT's perspective': 'Not programmable money, but programmable payments'; identity among surroundings; DTL contributions: inclusion, complementary channel, uniformity, innovation base.

title: Annual Report 2024 (DTL passages)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
content_note: Phase 2 R&D areas include digital identity integration, programmable payments, token-based systems, offline payments, cryptology and impact simulation.

title: Digital Turkish Lira: Benefits and Opportunities (CBRT Blog)
issuer: CBRT staff (Aşkaroğlu, Karayel, Öz, Tunalı) on CBRT Blog
relevance: objectives; distribution model (two-tier, no bank account needed); programmability layer; offline; optional use
content_note: Staff blog: two-tier model without requiring a bank account; separate programmability layer for licensed actors; legal-tender DTL usable offline; use 'optional rather than mandatory'. staff_research.

title: Press Release on Call to Join the Digital Turkish Lira Project Ecosystem (2025-46)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
content_note: CBRT 'considers digital money an important component of the financial technologies ecosystem'; DTL as building block for innovative uses; banks and payment/e-money institutions invited to sandbox.

title: Dijital Türk Lirası Projesi Ekosistemine Katılım Çağrısı (Call to Join the DTL Project Ecosystem, call document)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (Payment Systems and Financial Technologies Dept.)
relevance: programmability; identity (self-sovereign identity); tokenization; offline/GSM payments; objectives
content_note: DTL presented as complement to existing payments; categories: tokenization, programmable payments, self-sovereign identity, interoperability (POS, wallets, GSM), machine-to-machine payments.

title: Dijital Türk Lirası İkinci Faz İlerleme Raporuna İlişkin Basın Duyurusu (2025-59)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
content_note: Phase 2 continues; current status of programmable payments, offline payments and interoperability shared in Phase 2 Progress Report. Cover note for registry report.

title: Press Release on the Application Results of the Call to Join the Digital Turkish Lira Project Ecosystem (2026-33)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
content_note: 23 projects from 12 banks and 6 payment/e-money institutions enter sandbox stage: 17 programmable payments, 15 tokenization, 7 self-sovereign identity, 15 interoperability.

title: 理監事會後記者會參考資料：國際間央行數位貨幣最新發展與本行研究規劃進度
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: Sets CBDC principles (do no harm, legal basis), core features incl. offline transactions, consumer and privacy protection; reports domestic industry survey and CBC two-phase research plan.

title: 中央銀行專題報告「中央銀行數位貨幣(CBDC)整備狀況，以及如何因應加密貨幣跨入金融市場」(Special report to Legislative Yuan: CBDC readiness)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
relevance: objectives; privacy; offline; programmability; ledger technology; legal basis
content_note: Design considerations: protect privacy, always available, support offline transactions, programmable money; DLT limits; legal basis with AML/CFT and privacy rules; issuance not a race.

title: 金融穩定報告111年5月 專欄4：國際間CBDC發展趨勢及其政策意涵 (FSR May 2022, Box 4)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: CBDC 'not necessarily optimal for every country'; designs would protect consumer privacy while meeting AML rules; issuance must fit domestic needs, not a race.

title: 楊總裁專題演講「數位轉型的央行貨幣」(Governor Yang speech at FISC annual conference)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (Governor)
relevance: pilot results; ledger technology; two-tier; status
content_note: Phase-2 general-purpose CBDC trial done; DLT could not meet performance, so architecture centralised with some DLT functions; CBC distributes to banks, banks to public; next: survey, communication, law.

title: 中央銀行業務報告 (Business report to Legislative Yuan, Sep 2022)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: Phase-2 general-purpose CBDC trial completed June 2022; next: opinion survey, broad communication, more robust platform technology, legal framework; issuance not a race.

title: 中央銀行業務報告 (Business report to Legislative Yuan Finance Committee, Mar 2023)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: Trials assessing privacy, performance, security, traceability found 'DLT not superior to current centralised systems'; legal framework needed incl. legal tender, AML/CFT, privacy protection.

title: 理監事會後記者會參考資料：本行數位貨幣(CBDC)議題委外問卷調查結果之說明 (MPC press-conference note: CBDC survey results)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)

title: 中央銀行專題報告「數位貨幣發行之規劃與貨幣之數位轉型」(Special report to Legislative Yuan Finance Committee: planning of digital currency issuance)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
relevance: tiered wallets; privacy/data protection; holding limits; interest; two-tier distribution
content_note: Planned design: two-tier issuance; non-interest initially; wallets 'divided into anonymous and named wallets' with platform holding/transaction caps; named wallets need KYC; privacy rules.

title: 理監事會後記者會參考資料：資產代幣化世界之數位貨幣體系：存款代幣、穩定幣及央行數位貨幣(CBDC)扮演的角色
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)

title: 中央銀行業務報告 (Business report to Legislative Yuan Finance Committee, Oct 2025)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: Trial completed; 'no urgency to issue CBDC'; prototype becomes digital public-infrastructure payment platform for government vouchers; legal rules under study incl. privacy; cash protects privacy.

title: 中央銀行業務報告 (Business report to Legislative Yuan Finance Committee, Mar 2026)
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: 'No urgency to issue a retail CBDC'; prototype-based digital payment platform used for Hakka coins and NT$10,000 universal cash handout; focus shifts to wholesale CBDC for tokenization.

title: 新聞稿：發布「央行數位貨幣(CBDC)對外溝通活動總結報告」
issuer: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
content_note: Releases summary of 2025 hearings (9 events, 1,714 participants); concerns incl. policy objectives, legal basis, system architecture, risk/security/privacy. Cover for registry report.

title: Fintech Development Strategy of Ukraine until 2025
content_note: Action plan lists 'Launch of CBDC project' and task '(i) issue e-hryvnia (CBDC)', NBU with Ministry of Digital Transformation, 2020-2021.

title: Report on the results of the International Conference CBDCinUA2020
content_note: Governor Smolii: NBU ran blockchain-based e-hryvnia pilot, e-hryvnia as digital equivalent of cash; NBU 'will be ready to return to this matter'; mandate not impaired.

title: Strategy of Ukrainian Financial Sector Development until 2025
issuer: National Bank of Ukraine with financial regulators and Ministry of Finance
content_note: States the E-Hryvnia pilot was carried out and 'a concept for the use of the e-hryvnia (CBDC) at the national level has been developed'.

title: Law of Ukraine 'On Payment Services' No. 1591-IX (defines NBU digital money / e-hryvnia)
content_note: Defines e-hryvnia as electronic form of the national currency issued by the NBU (cited by NBU FAQ/news). Rada site unreachable from here; text not opened.

title: Survey Results on the Possibility of E-hryvnia Implementation
content_note: Expert survey: 'most respondents support the anonymity of individual users'; 80% chose users may remain anonymous; offline payments for sub-limit amounts with anonymous tokens.

title: National Bank welcomes the Ministry of Digital Transformation pilot on programmable e-money (news, incl. e-hryvnia plan)
relevance: status (concept by end-2022; tender 2023; decision later); programmability
content_note: Mintsyfra pilot not e-hryvnia; only NBU may issue e-hryvnia; concept due end-2022, then regulation, provider tender (2023) and test issue before deciding on full-scale issuance.

title: NBU Unveils E-hryvnia Concept to Payment Market and Virtual Asset Market Participants (news)
content_note: Concept presented for feedback; use cases: retail payments with 'programmed' money for targeted social benefits via smart contracts, virtual assets, cross-border; balanced approach to issuance.

title: Draft Vision of Introducing E-hryvnia (E-hryvnia: digital money of the National Bank of Ukraine)
relevance: privacy/data access; identifiability (identified wallets, anonymous wallets with limits); programmability; ledger technology; offline; two-tier
content_note: Draft for feedback: 'The NBU tracks fund flows across all wallets'; e-hryvnia wallets identified, 'anonymous wallets with limits are under consideration'; programmed state payouts; DLT vs non-DLT options.

title: E-hryvnia Q&A (FAQ section)
relevance: privacy/data access; offline; programmability; wallet recovery; legal tender
content_note: Key features: privacy and safety, payments secured by NBU 'while the regulator will not have any personal information'; offline payments; wallet access recovery; programmability; cash will not disappear.

title: Bank of England statement on Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC Taskforce)
issuer: Bank of England and HM Treasury
content_note: Joint CBDC Taskforce created; 'have not yet made a decision on whether to introduce a CBDC'; CBDC would exist alongside cash and deposits, not replace them.

title: New forms of digital money (Discussion Paper)
content_note: Box E on data and privacy; value in money that 'offers data protection and privacy'; Bank has not decided whether to introduce a CBDC.

title: Central Bank Digital Currency: an update on the Bank of England's work (speech by Tom Mutton)
content_note: 'We have not yet made a decision on whether or not one is needed'; 2020 DP responses stressed financial inclusion and privacy; programmability among functional considerations.

title: Statement on Central Bank Digital Currency next steps
issuer: HM Treasury and Bank of England
content_note: 'No decision has been made'; 2022 consultation to inform move to development phase; earliest launch second half of the decade.

title: Responses to the Discussion Paper on new forms of digital money
content_note: Summarises feedback on whether a CBDC should offer data protection and privacy; Bank 'has not yet made a decision' but strong support to continue.

title: HM Treasury and Bank of England consider plans for a digital pound (news story)
issuer: HM Treasury and Bank of England
relevance: identifiability; privacy; programmability; holding limits; ledger (platform model); status
content_note: Digital pound 'would not be anonymous'; rigorous privacy standards; 'Neither the Government nor Bank would program a digital pound'; holding limits; decision around mid-decade.

title: The digital pound: speech by Jon Cunliffe (UK Finance)
content_note: Taskforce concludes 'not yet at a point where a firm decision can be made'; 2-3 year design stage before decision; launch possible second half of decade.

title: What is the digital pound? (explainer with Q&A)
content_note: Q&A incl. 'Would the Government or the Bank of England be able to control or monitor my digital pounds?' and why holding limits are needed; answers partly in video.

title: Bank of England and HM Treasury respond to digital pound consultation (news story)
issuer: HM Treasury and Bank of England
content_note: Primary legislation 'would guarantee users' privacy and control'; 'The Bank and the government would not have access to any personal data'; no final decision; decide after design phase.

title: National Payments Vision (incl. section 'Exploring a potential digital pound')
content_note: Government will 'continue the design phase for a retail CBDC... in partnership with the Bank'; 'No decision has been taken on whether to implement a digital pound'.

title: Letter from Andrew Bailey to Dame Meg Hillier MP, Chair of the Treasury Committee
issuer: Bank of England (Governor), published by House of Commons Treasury Committee
content_note: 'No decision has been made on whether to proceed beyond the current design phase'; digital pound only after Parliament passes primary legislation; design-phase costs.

title: Digital Pound Lab: Phase 2 update
content_note: Phase 2 (Nov 2025 to Jul 2026) demos: one-time aliases let users 'conduct a transaction in private'; programmability features (locks) for conditional payments. Page last updated 6 Oct 2026.

title: El presidente del BCU expuso en el Instituto Uruguayo de Numismática (news; Labat talk on digital money)
content_note: Labat: a digital currency 'puede servir a Uruguay para apoyar la competencia, eficiencia e innovación en los pagos'; issuance decision requires infrastructure; refers to e-peso pilot.

title: Evolving payment ecosystems and CBDC: An ecological approach (A. Sarmiento)
issuer: BCU staff (Adolfo Sarmiento), published on BCU payment-system oversight page
content_note: Staff paper (author-views disclaimer): e-Peso pilot issuance capped at UYU 20m, 10,000 phone users, wallets limited to UYU 30,000; platform acted as registry of banknote ownership. staff_research.

title: El presidente del BCU reiteró la relevancia de construir un sistema de pagos que opere con celeridad (news; Labat at IMF/WB Annual Meetings)
relevance: status (pilot not scaled; new steps announced); objectives
content_note: Labat: 2017 pilot 'muy exitoso'; 'Todavía no hemos escalado el proyecto, pero... tendremos nuevos avances el año entrante'; priority is a fast payment system, no contradiction with CBDC.

title: BIS Innovation Hub and the South African Reserve Bank will test CBDCs for international settlements (Project Dunbar) - WHOLESALE
content_note: Announces Project Dunbar multi-CBDC platform for cross-border settlement with BIS Innovation Hub; wholesale only.

title: SARB retail CBDC Background Note (companion to the Position Paper; reports the 2021-22 retail CBDC feasibility study)
relevance: feasibility study results; ledger/architecture (single- vs two-tier); privacy; offline; programmability
content_note: Reports 2021 feasibility study of a SARB digital currency as electronic legal tender complementary to cash; two two-tier deployment models tested; discusses privacy vs cash, offline and programmability.

title: SARB position paper on the necessity of a retail CBDC in South Africa (publication notice / landing page)
content_note: Retail CBDC 'technically feasible' but 'no compelling immediate need for its implementation'; priority is payments modernisation; SARB to pivot toward wholesale CBDC.
